title: Part 5 analysis.json (simon.analysis.v1)
description: Part 5's output for Part 7. The fields of 1.0 plus the optional additions of 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 (schema_version, status, phrasing, faults[].joints, runs, coaching, diagnostics.guard; 1.2.0: faults[].follower_t_s, at_s, follower_runs, lateral, lateral_m, text_timed and the top-level score; 1.3.0: faults[].reps, diagnostics.guard.reps, diagnostics.expected_reference and score.per_rep, for a take compared one repetition at a time). A document without them keeps schema_version 1.2.0. A 1.0 document validates. Read status before faults: a refused take has status.code different_movement and faults []. Extra fields are allowed. 1.4.0 (ADR-0012): a take is always analysed. status.code is ok for every analysis; what used to be a refusal is an entry in the top-level warnings ([{code, text}]: low_match, moving_part_out_of_frame, not_enough_visible, no_usable_measures), with match ({quality ok|low, residual, timing_corr, limits}); on a low match each fault has confidence "low"; score is never null, is capped at 59 (grade F) when any warning is present, and then names the codes in score.capped_by. A document without warnings keeps its earlier schema_version. 1.5.0 (ADR-0014): every new document is 1.5.0 and carries cues: faults[].cue and cue_kind (position or range), the same on each score.timeline[].misses[] with its direction, score.timeline[].tempo and score.tempo ({ratio, cue}: follower seconds per example second, a cue below 0.85 or above 1.15), and the top-level insights (at most 5, ranked by the points they cost the score). 1.6.0 (ADR-0015): every new document is 1.6.0 and may carry the foot measures: faults with measure foot_rotation or ankle_inversion (body_part feet, joint an ankle, cue and words like any fault) and diagnostics.feet, written only when a feet file (Part 2 pose3d.json with extra_joints) was given for either clip. A document without them is exactly what 1.5.0 was apart from schema_version. 1.7.0 (ADR-0016): every new document is 1.7.0 and carries profile, the analysis profile that produced it (a non-empty string; the names are data in part5/profiles.json, today dance, rehab and fitness, fitness being the default and the unchanged analysis). A score is read within its profile. Under the dance profile only, score.components and each window's components carry tempo (points the take's pace cost) and the tempo insight's points equal it. A document before 1.7.0 has no profile and is read as fitness. The earlier field groups stay optional and are told apart by their fields. 1.8.0 (TICKET-043): every new document is 1.8.0 and may carry diagnostics.near_misses, the candidate faults detection considered and dropped: {total, omitted, items}, the items the largest first and at most 10, each a measure, side and direction with a frame past its threshold that failed persistence (reason persistence, with shortfall_frames) or was explained by a kept fault (reason explained_by); a take compared rep by rep adds the reasons reps and fitness. It is present whenever the take was compared (also with total 0) and absent when it could not be aligned. It changes no fault or score, is for people debugging a take and is not shown to the follower. 1.9.0 (TICKET-045, TICKET-046, docs/specs/second-opinion.md): every new document is 1.9.0. phrasing carries lang (the language of the fault lines, a listed BCP 47 primary subtag, en by default) and lang_requested when the request named a tag that is not listed as given; each phrasing.faults[] entry carries text (the line shown, equal to the fault's coaching) and lang (the line's own language: en for a line that fell back to the template). The optional top-level second_opinion is written when clips were given: Muse Spark's view of the take, labelled model_opinion and never read by the score, faults or insights; status ok, fallback (reason says why) or skipped (not attempted), per-fault verdicts {fault_index, agrees, note} and at most 2 observations {at_s, text, label}. The same 1.9.0 also carries score.uncapped ({value, grade}, Part 7 TICKET-155: the value and grade before the warning cap, present only when the cap lowered the value) and TICKET-048: the optional top-level source (the producing part; absent means part5) and the warnings code no_person, written only by Part 7's own analysis when Part 2 finds nobody in the take (schema_version 1.4.0 or later, source part7, faults [], score 0 F, no match). 1.10.0 (TICKET-047, ADR-0018): every new document is 1.10.0. score.version may be simon.score.v2, in which a miss costs less on a measure the trainer moves little in its window (never below a floor) and a take whose faults list is not empty is capped at 89: score.fault_cap (the integer 89, present only when the take reports a fault) says so, and score.uncapped is the value and grade before every cap, the fault cap and the warning cap. score.capped_by is unchanged: it names the warning codes of the low-match cap at 59 and never the fault cap. A 1.9.0 document and every earlier one still validates. 1.11.0 (TICKET-060, ADR-0019): every new document is 1.11.0. score.version may be simon.score.v3, which keeps the weight and the cap of v2 for a take that reports one fault and caps a take whose faults list holds two or more entries at 79: score.fault_cap is the ceiling in force (89 or 79; read it, never assume 89), and score.uncapped and score.capped_by mean what they meant in 1.10.0. A 1.10.0 document and every earlier one still validates. Correction (TICKET-073): the rehab profile has written the tempo cue "Slower is fine" for a ratio above 1.15 since 1.7.0 (ADR-0016), and the cue enums of score.tempo and score.timeline[].tempo omitted it; they now list it. The schema_version does not change: the documents did not change, only the schema's list of what they may say. 1.12.0 (TICKET-071, docs/specs/history-per-rep.md): every new document is 1.12.0 and adds three fields for comparing takes with each other. A fault of a take compared rep by rep carries rep_sizes, one {rep, magnitude_deg, side, body_part} for each rep in reps: the fault's size in that rep, signed like magnitude_deg, and the side that rep found it on (both when it found both sides). Each score.per_rep entry carries rep (the follower rep's index, which is the position of its window in score.timeline) and tempo_ratio (that window's tempo.ratio, follower seconds per example second, null where the rep could not be timed and null for every rep of a low match). Each diagnostics.near_misses item carries margin_deg, abs(magnitude_deg) minus threshold_deg to 0.1 degree: positive when the candidate went past the threshold by that much, 0 when it sat on it, negative when it stayed short of it. Detection lists only candidates with a frame past the threshold, so today margin_deg is 0 or more. A fault, the score and the insights read none of the three. A 1.11.0 document and every earlier one still validates. 1.13.0 (ADR-0020): every new document is 1.13.0 and its score carries credit (simon.credit.v1), a DDR-style display beside the score: every measure seen in at least half of a compared window's frames earns, on each frame it is measured, 1.0, 0.6 or 0.2 when the follower is within 0.5, 1 or 2 detection thresholds of the example (times the level's tolerance), else 0. percent is the credit earned over the credit possible, points count 100 per measure per second, at the levels easy, normal and hard, and per_window has one entry per compared window of score.timeline. score.credit is null when nothing was compared. Additive: value, grade, components, the caps and every other field are unchanged, the warning cap does not apply to credit, and nothing reads it back. A 1.12.0 document and every earlier one still validates. 1.14.0 (TICKET-084, ADR-0023; TICKET-080, docs/specs/language-cues.md): every new document is 1.14.0. It carries body_mask when the follower declared limb chains that are not scored (part5 analyse --mask, the mask field of POST api/analyse): every measure that reads a masked joint is dropped from detection and the score after alignment, so no fault, miss, insight or near miss names it and the score is taken on the remaining measures. For a request in a listed language other than English, phrasing carries cues (one {path, text, lang, backend, model, fallback_reason} for each cue and reason of the document, written by the model in that language in one batched call, or the field's English text with the reason it was not taken) and native_review (false until a native reader has checked the language); the English cue fields, coaching, the score and the insights are unchanged by them. A document without body_mask, phrasing.cues and phrasing.native_review is what 1.13.0 was apart from schema_version and quality.signals.heading_offset_deg (with its reason past 5 degrees). The quality block gains signals.heading_offset_deg and the reason heading_offset (TICKET-086), the heading left between the example and the follower over the aligned frames, reported only like the rest of the block. A 1.13.0 document and every earlier one still validates.

source.description: 1.9.0 (TICKET-048): the part that produced this document, part5 or part7 today. Absent means part5, so every document Part 5 writes omits it. Part 7 writes part7 on the analysis it makes itself when Part 2 finds nobody in the take (warnings code no_person).

profile.description: 1.7.0 (ADR-0016): the analysis profile that produced this document, one of the names in part5/profiles.json (dance, rehab, fitness). Always present from 1.7.0; a document without it is read as fitness. Scores compare within one profile.

body_mask.description: 1.14.0 (TICKET-084, ADR-0023): the limb chains the follower declared not scored: seated (both legs), or not using an arm from the shoulder, a forearm from the elbow or a leg from the hip. Written only when a mask was declared; absent means the whole body was scored. Every measure that reads a masked joint is dropped on every frame of both clips from detection and the score, after alignment (timing and the guard read the whole body): no fault, timeline miss, insight or near miss names it, and the score is taken on the remaining measures, so it compares only with takes under the same mask. Show text beside the score and dim the not scored chains. Designed for and tested on seated and masked takes from the fixtures, not with wheelchair users or amputees.

declared.description: The presets and chains as declared, each once, in the order given. full_body masks nothing and stands alone.

source.description: Where the mask came from: part5 analyse --mask, or the mask field of POST api/analyse.

scored_chains.description: The chains with at least one measure scored, in the order left_arm, right_arm, left_forearm, right_forearm, left_leg, right_leg; an arm whose forearm alone is masked is here. With not_scored_chains it lists every chain once.

not_scored_chains.description: The chains whose every measure is dropped, in the same order; a masked arm lists its forearm too.

masked_joints.description: The canonical joints masked (left_elbow, left_wrist and so on), the subject's own sides; a leg also masks the heel and toes of a feet file, which are not listed. Dim the bones that end at these joints.

not_scored_measures.description: The sided body and foot measures dropped (left_elbow_flexion, right_foot_rotation and so on): no fault, miss, insight or near miss of the document names one.

text.description: The plain words to show: "Legs not scored, by your setting.", "Left arm and right leg not scored, by your setting."; "Whole body scored, by your setting." for full_body.

code.description: ok for every analysis from 1.4.0; the other values only in documents written before ADR-0012.

faults.description: Sorted by absolute magnitude, largest first. Empty for a correct take, for a refusal in a document before 1.4.0, and when nothing was detected.

text.description: 1.9.0: the line shown for this fault (equal to the fault's coaching).

lang.description: 1.9.0: this line's language; en when it fell back to the template.
1.9.0 (TICKET-046): the language the lines were asked in (en by default).

lang_requested.description: 1.9.0: the tag the request named when it differs from lang (a region tag, or a language Part 5 does not list).

cues.description: 1.14.0 (TICKET-080, docs/specs/language-cues.md): written only when lang is a listed language other than en. One entry for each cue and reason of the document, in document order: faults[].cue, each timeline window's misses[].cue and tempo.cue, score.tempo.cue, then each insight's cue and why. The English fields themselves do not change; text is what to show in the follower's language. An entry the model wrote has the model's text, lang the requested language, backend and model of the writer and fallback_reason null. An entry that failed its word test, or whose backend could not run, keeps the field's English text with lang en, backend template, model null and the reason. [] when the document has none.

path.description: 1.14.0: the field this entry is about, such as faults[0].cue, score.timeline[2].misses[0].cue, score.timeline[2].tempo.cue, score.tempo.cue, insights[1].cue or insights[1].why.

text.description: 1.14.0: the cue or reason to show, in lang.

lang.description: 1.14.0: the language of text: the requested language, or en for a fallback.

backend.description: 1.14.0: who wrote text; template for a fallback.

model.description: 1.14.0: the model that wrote text, null for a fallback.

fallback_reason.description: 1.14.0: null when the model wrote text, else why the English text is shown (never a key or the model's text).

native_review.description: 1.14.0 (TICKET-080): written when lang is a listed language other than en. false until a native reader has checked the language (none has), so a viewer can say the text has not been reviewed by a native reader.

reps.description: 1.3.0: one entry per follower repetition: its start and end on the follower file's clock, the guard's numbers for it (null when it could not be aligned) and whether it passed.

expected_reference.description: 1.3.0: which part of the expected clip the follower repetitions were compared with: kind first_rep (its first complete repetition) or whole (it holds one).

visibility.description: 1.3.0: present when the take was compared on fewer measures than the full body because the camera did not see the rest (ADR-0011): usable_measures (how many), excluded (the measures left out) and rule (the sentence that decided).

moving_measures.description: Measures that move in the expected clip (robust range above 20 degrees) among those the example shows.

moving_usable.description: Those of moving_measures the take also shows; none of them means status moving_part_out_of_frame.

feet.description: 1.6.0 (ADR-0015): present when a feet file (Part 2 pose3d.json with extra_joints, --expected-feet / --follower-feet) was given for either clip. expected and follower say where each clip's foot points came from, how many of the clip's frames matched a frame of that file in time and which foot measures were seen in at least 80% of them (usable). compared lists the foot measures the pair was compared on (usable on both sides); hidden_reason is null when any was compared and otherwise says why none was (no file, a file with no foot points, too few frames seen, rep mode).

near_misses.description: 1.8.0 (TICKET-043): the candidate faults detection considered and dropped. total is how many there are, items the largest by abs(magnitude_deg) (at most 10) and omitted the rest. A take compared rep by rep lists them at the take level, like its faults.

score.description: simon.score.v1, simon.score.v2 from 1.10.0 (ADR-0018) or simon.score.v3 from 1.11.0 (ADR-0019). Never null from 1.4.0 (0, grade F when nothing could be measured); capped at 59 with capped_by when the document has warnings. From v2 a take that reports a fault is also capped at 89, with fault_cap; under v3 a take that reports two or more faults is capped at 79. null only in a refused document of 1.3.0 or earlier. Absent when the producer does not score.

tempo.description: 1.7.0 (ADR-0016): points the take's pace cost; present under the dance profile only.

per_rep.description: 1.3.0: the value and grade of each accepted repetition; the score is their mean (components are the means), before any cap: the value of a simon.score.v2 or v3 take that reports a fault is at most fault_cap, and uncapped then holds the mean.

rep.description: 1.12.0 (TICKET-071): the follower repetition (0-based) this entry is for, which is the position of its window in timeline and the rep in faults[].reps and faults[].rep_sizes[].rep. Entries list the accepted reps only, so rep is the way to join them to a fault.

tempo_ratio.description: 1.12.0 (TICKET-071): that rep's tempo, follower seconds per example second, equal to the tempo.ratio of timeline[rep]. null where the rep could not be timed (the example's rep is under 1 s) and for every rep of a low match (match.quality low, TICKET-063): not measured, never on time.

capped_by.description: 1.4.0: the warning codes that capped the value at 59. Only the low-match warning cap is named here; the fault cap of simon.score.v2 and v3 is never in this list (see fault_cap).

fault_cap.description: 1.10.0 (TICKET-047, ADR-0018), simon.score.v2 and v3 only: the highest value a take that reports a fault can score, the ceiling in force. Under v2 it is 89 (the top of B) for any reported fault; under v3 (1.11.0, ADR-0019) it is 89 for a take that reports one fault and 79 (the top of C) for a take whose faults list holds two or more entries. Present when the take's faults list is not empty, whether or not the cap lowered this value; absent for a take with no faults and under simon.score.v1. When it lowered the value, uncapped holds the value before it. It is not a warning: capped_by does not name it. Like capped_by, it lowers the take's value (the mean of the timeline's compared windows) and never a window's value.

uncapped.description: 1.9.0 (Part 7 TICKET-155): the value and grade before the warning cap; present only when the cap lowered the value, so a reader can say what the warning cost. From 1.10.0 it is the value and grade before every cap, the fault cap of simon.score.v2 or v3 (fault_cap, 89 or 79) and the warning cap (capped_by): present when either lowered the value, and when both did it is the value before the first. A faulted take with no warning that the fault cap lowered has uncapped and no capped_by. Never read back by the score.

basis.description: ADR-0013: what the timeline's windows are: about 5 s slices of a take compared as a whole, or its repetitions.

timeline.description: ADR-0013: the take window by window. value is the mean of the compared windows; each window's value is 100 minus its misses' points and its similarity component.

cue.description: 1.5.0 (ADR-0014): what to do, an imperative of at most 6 words from measure, direction and side (template text, never rewritten by a phrasing backend).

cue_kind.description: 1.5.0: range when the fix is how far a joint bends or a limb lifts, position when it is where a body part is placed or how it is aligned.

enum: Slow down to match the trainer
Speed up to match the trainer

tempo.description: 1.5.0: the window's tempo, on compared windows. 1.5.0: follower seconds per example second (null when the example side spans under 1 s); cue below 0.85 or above 1.15, else null. The cue is one of the two default cues, or the rehab profile's "Slower is fine" for a ratio above 1.15 (ADR-0016; TICKET-073 corrects the enum, which had omitted the rehab cue the producer has written since 1.7.0; no schema_version change).

enum: Slow down to match the trainer
Speed up to match the trainer

tempo.description: 1.5.0: the take's tempo: the whole take, or the median of its reps. 1.5.0: follower seconds per example second (null when the example side spans under 1 s); cue below 0.85 or above 1.15, else null. The cue is one of the two default cues, or the rehab profile's "Slower is fine" for a ratio above 1.15 (ADR-0016; TICKET-073 corrects the enum, which had omitted the rehab cue the producer has written since 1.7.0; no schema_version change).

credit.description: 1.13.0 (ADR-0020): the DDR-style credit display, simon.credit.v1, additive beside the score (value, grade and the caps are unchanged, and the warning cap of 59 does not apply here). Per compared window of timeline, each measure finite in at least half of the window's frames earns on each frame it is finite the credit of the first band [z_max, credit] of bands that z / tolerance is within (z = |follower - expected| / detection threshold), else 0. points = credit * 100 per measure per second, a frame lasting what it does on the example's clock (so, within one comparison basis, the whole take or rep by rep, and with the same measures seen, the same routine has the same max_points however fast the follower was), times the level's multiplier, summed over windows; max_points the same at credit 1. percent = 100 * points / max_points, to 0.1, and grade is the percent's own letter on the credit's own scale, grades (S 95, A 85, B 75, C 65, D 55, E 40, F under 40; informational, never score.grade). The top-level percent, points and max_points are those of the level named by tolerance. null when nothing was compared (no alignment, no compared window, or no measure that could be counted). Only the body measures earn credit; the foot measures are compared but earn none. From Part 5 1.14.2 (TICKET-108, ADR-0020 Amendment 1; the schema is unchanged): over the example's last second of the take (at most a third of the expected frames read; rep by rep, the last rep), when the follower holds still (every measure read within half a threshold), each measure the example moves away in (at least one threshold) earns full credit on every counted entry of that second; max_points is unchanged. Absent in a document before 1.13.0.

grade.description: Informational: the letter for percent on the credit's own scale, grades (S to F; not the score's bands). It is not score.grade, it sets no cap and no gate, and it ignores warnings and caps, so a take capped to F can carry a credit grade of B. Part 5's validator also checks what this schema cannot: grade is the letter percent reaches on this document's grades (the first entry whose percent at least it reaches, else the last entry's letter), so a grade that does not match its percent is refused.

tolerance.description: The level the top-level percent, points and max_points are shown at (normal: tolerance x1.0, points x1.0; easy: x1.5, x0.75; hard: x0.7, x1.5).

bands.description: [z / tolerance at most, credit] from the tightest band; beyond the last the credit is 0.

per_window.description: One entry per compared window of timeline, same t_s, same order, at the level named by tolerance.

grades.description: The credit's letter grades: [percent at least, grade], highest first (Part 5 writes S 95 down to F at 0, so every percent under 40 is F; ADR-0020). Part 5's validator also checks what this schema cannot: the list is not empty, each percent is below the one before (the marks fall), and the letters run in the scale's order S, A, B, C, D, E, F, each later than the one before, so no letter appears twice. Rank the letters by that order, never by the alphabet.

warnings.description: 1.4.0: why the grade is capped at F; present only when the take had a warning. A document with no_person alone (1.9.0) has no match, because nothing was compared.

code.description: no_person (1.9.0, TICKET-048): Part 2 found no person in the take; produced only by Part 7's own analysis (source part7), never by Part 5.

match.description: 1.4.0: how closely the take matches the trainer's movement; present with warnings. quality is low when the guard would have refused.

quality.description: 1.13.0 (TICKET-079, ADR-0021): how well the camera saw the follower's take, simon.quality.v1. Optional: detect it by presence, and read a document without it as not assessed (every document before 1.13.0). level is ok, degraded or major; reasons says why (a closed list of codes, each with plain words, the reading as value, the limit it crossed as threshold and, where one joint is the cause, that joint); signals holds the raw readings, null when a reading cannot be made and never 0 in its place; score_cap is 59 when level is major, else null. Reported only: score.value, score.grade, score.fault_cap, score.uncapped, score.capped_by and warnings are what they are without it, it never adds a warnings entry, and low_match is not one of its reasons. A take that carries the warning not_enough_visible, moving_part_out_of_frame or no_usable_measures is major with that reason. Part 7 applies the cap.

insights.description: 1.5.0 (ADR-0014): what to work on first. With a score timeline, one item per distinct cue among the misses, ranked by points (their share of the score: summed over the compared windows, divided by their number); at_s and window are the cue's first miss. A tempo item (points null) is added last and kept when score.tempo has a cue, except a reassurance: under the rehab profile a slow take has the cue "Slower is fine" in score.tempo and no tempo item, because this list holds actions (ADR-0016, amendment 2). Without a timeline, one item per distinct fault cue in the order of faults, points null.

cue.description: 1.5.0 (ADR-0014): what to do, an imperative of at most 6 words from measure, direction and side (template text, never rewritten by a phrasing backend).

second_opinion.description: 1.9.0 (TICKET-045, contract C1): Muse Spark 1.3's second opinion, from one call that watched the teacher's recording and the student's take with the measured faults. The model's view: label it as such. The score, faults and insights never read it. Absent when no clip was given.

status.description: ok: the model answered; fallback: a call was prepared or made and failed; skipped: not attempted (one clip, no key, live off).

reason.description: Why it is not ok; null when ok.

lang.description: The language of note and text (en).

rejected.description: Items the guardrail dropped, with the reason; for debugging.

usage.description: Tokens and USD of the call, at list rates.

then.$comment: documents written before ADR-0012 (1.3.0 and earlier): a refusal has no faults

level.description: The worst reason: ok when there is none, degraded when the worst is at its degraded limit, major when it is at its major limit or the take carries not_enough_visible, moving_part_out_of_frame or no_usable_measures.

reasons.description: Empty for ok. In a fixed order: the three warning reasons, then joints_unseen, joints_missing, frames_missing, measures_hidden, position_jitter, heading_offset (1.14.0). Each signal gives at most one reason, at the higher limit it reached.

code.description: The first three repeat the warning of the same code and carry no number. joints_unseen, joints_missing, frames_missing and measures_hidden read the share signals of the same names, position_jitter reads position_jitter_mm, heading_offset (1.14.0, TICKET-086) reads heading_offset_deg.

words.description: One plain sentence made from the measured numbers. It names no cause (light, a hand in front of the lens): Part 5 has no reading for one.

value.description: The reading of the signal behind the reason, in that signal's unit; null for a warning reason.

threshold.description: The limit the reading reached (the degraded or the major limit of part5/quality.json), in the signal's unit; null for a warning reason.

joint.description: Optional: the joint with the largest reading, on joints_unseen, joints_missing and position_jitter. A canonical joint name, the performer's own left and right.

signals.description: The raw readings from the follower's file as Part 5 loads it, before smoothing, and from 1.14.0 heading_offset_deg, read after alignment. null when a reading cannot be made; never 0 in its place (0 is a measured zero). heading_offset_deg is written in every document from 1.14.0 and is absent before it.

unseen_joint_share.description: Share of the joint readings at Part 2's 0.3 unseen mark, counted as ADR-0011 counts it: a joint is unseen when its left or right counterpart is at 0.3 too (the nose when it is). Only the joints the example itself sees in at least half of its frames are counted, read from the example's own conf or --expected-visibility the way ADR-0011 reads them, and the share is over the readings of those joints; an example of unknown visibility (no conf anywhere, such as a Part 4 animation) counts every joint. Null when the follower file carries no conf, or the example sees no joint.

missing_joint_share.description: Share of the joint readings that are null or have conf below 0.3.

missing_frame_share.description: Share of the frames that are flagged interpolated or have at most half of the 17 joints usable.

hidden_measure_share.description: Share of the full-body measures the example shows that the follower's own conf makes unusable under ADR-0011 (a joint seen in fewer than 80 percent of the frames). A measure the example shows is one whose every joint the example sees (its own conf or --expected-visibility); with the example's visibility unknown that is all 22. From Part 5 1.14.2 (TICKET-107; the schema is unchanged) a measure the example does not show is not counted: it is not applicable, so it is not left out of the take. Null when the file carries no conf or the example shows no full-body measure.

position_jitter_mm.description: Frame-to-frame jitter of the joint positions in millimetres per frame: per joint and axis, feet.jitter (the median absolute change between consecutive frames) of the step series, so a steady movement is not jitter; the three axes joined as a norm; the median over the joints. It depends on the file's frame rate. Null when no joint has enough frames.

heading_offset_deg.description: 1.14.0 (TICKET-086): the heading left between the example and the follower after Part 3's facing step, in degrees. In each aligned frame pair (example frame i and the follower frame exp_to_fol[i]; every aligned rep of a take compared rep by rep) the body's heading is the direction, in the horizontal plane, of the hip line and the shoulder line (left minus right, each made unit length and added); the signal is the median over the pairs of the angle between the two headings, 0 to 180. Null when the take could not be aligned or no pair has a hip or shoulder line to read. TICKET-082 measured that a turned follower moves the score (5 degrees moved 18 of 54 seed 5 scores by up to 10 points, 15 degrees moved 43 by up to 34): a take past the degraded limit was filmed from another angle than the example, so treat its score as rough.

score_cap.description: 59 (score.WARNING_CAP, the cap a warning puts on score.value) when level is major, else null. Reported only: Part 5 does not apply it, Part 7 does.

foot_measure.description: 1.6.0: a foot measure by its sided name; a fault names it side-less (foot_rotation, ankle_inversion).

feet_side.description: 1.6.0: one clip's feet file. source is the path given, null when none was; person the people[].id read; frames_matched how many of the clip's frames took a frame of the file within half its median frame step over all its frames (at least 0.008 s); usable the foot measures seen in at least 80% of the clip's frames.

measure.description: What differed, side-less (upper_arm_out, knee_flexion, ...). 1.6.0: foot_rotation and ankle_inversion, only when the pair has foot points (diagnostics.feet).

joint.description: Where it differed. A sided joint, a side-stripped joint for side both, or spine, shoulders or neck for centre measures.

direction.description: More or less than the example.

confidence.description: A number in 0..1, or "low" on a low match (1.4.0).

runs.description: Every counted run, in expected frames. Optional (schema 1.1.0).

follower_t_s.description: Seconds on the follower file's own clock at follower_frames[0] and [1].

at_s.description: follower_t_s[0] rounded half up to 0.1 s.

follower_runs.description: Every run in follower file frames, same order as runs.

lateral.description: Which way the part is off, in the subject's own frame (like side); null when no direction applies.

lateral_m.description: foot_out on one side only: metres further out (positive) than the example.

text_timed.description: The timed words plus ' at <at_s> s'.

reps.description: 1.3.0: the follower repetitions (0-based, in order) this fault was found in; at_s, follower_t_s and follower_runs are those of the first.

rep_sizes.description: 1.12.0 (TICKET-071): the fault's size in each rep that found it, for a take compared rep by rep; one entry for each rep in reps, in the same order. Absent on a take compared as a whole.

rep.description: The follower repetition (0-based), the same index as in reps and in score.per_rep[].rep.

magnitude_deg.description: The fault's size in that rep, signed like the fault's magnitude_deg (more positive, less negative). A rep that found both sides gives the mean of the two.

side.description: The side that rep found the fault on. It can differ from the fault's own side: a fault reported on the left side counts a rep that found both sides, and one reported on both counts a rep that found one.

body_part.description: The body part of that rep's occurrence; the fault's body_part for the same measure.

cue.description: 1.5.0 (ADR-0014): what to do, an imperative of at most 6 words from measure, direction and side (template text, never rewritten by a phrasing backend).

cue_kind.description: 1.5.0: range when the fix is how far a joint bends or a limb lifts, position when it is where a body part is placed or how it is aligned.

near_miss.description: A measure on one side in one direction with at least one frame past its threshold that was not reported, sized like a fault. Sides are never merged: side is left, right or center.

magnitude_deg.description: Signed median of the smoothed difference over the counted runs, else over every frame past the threshold.

margin_deg.description: 1.12.0 (TICKET-071): abs(magnitude_deg) minus threshold_deg, to 0.1 degree, whatever the direction. Positive: the candidate went past the threshold by that many degrees before persistence (or the rep count) dropped it. 0: it sat on the threshold. Negative: it stayed short of the threshold by that many degrees. Detection lists only candidates with a frame past the threshold, so today the value is 0 or more; the negative sign is defined so a reader never has to guess it.

expected_frames.description: The longest run past the threshold, expected-clip frames (on the expected file's frames in rep mode).

follower_frames.description: The matched frames of the follower file for that run.

frames_over.description: Frames past the threshold, any run length.

counted_frames.description: Those in runs of at least min_run_frames: what persistence counts.

needed_frames.description: What persistence needed: max(min_frames_floor, round(min_fraction x clip frames)).

reason.description: persistence: too few counted frames. explained_by: a kept fault explains it. reps (rep mode): reported in some reps but fewer than half. fitness (rep mode, profile): half the reps reported it and the profile's take-level check dropped it.

explained_by.description: reason explained_by: the kept fault that explains it, as that fault is reported.

reps.description: Rep mode: the follower repetitions (0-based) in which it crossed the threshold.

found_in_reps.description: Rep mode, reason reps or fitness: the most reps that reported one exact side of it.

needed_reps.description: Rep mode, reason reps or fitness: half the accepted reps, rounded up.

percent.description: 100 * points / max_points, to 0.1; null only when max_points is 0.

credit_entry.description: The three numbers every credit level and every per-window entry carries: percent, points and max_points, with percent = 100 * points / max_points.
